# 1 Maccabees Chapter 14 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 14 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_014_page_001.jpg

---

**1** In the one hundred and seventy-second year King Demetrius assembled his forces and marched into Media to obtain auxiliary forces to use against Trypho.

**2** When Arsaces the king of Persia and Media heard that Demetrius had entered his territories, he sent one of his commanders to take him alive.

**3** The commander marched out, defeated Demetrius's army, seized him, and brought him to Arsaces, who kept him under guard.

**4** The land of Judea was at peace all the days of Simon. He sought the welfare of his people, and his authority and renown pleased them all his days.

---

*[The following verses, 4b–15, constitute an encomium or praise-poem embedded in the prose narrative. It is structured in parallelisms characteristic of biblical poetry.]*

**5** Among his glorious achievements was this: he took Joppa for a harbor
    and opened access to the islands of the sea.

**6** He enlarged the borders of his nation
    and gained mastery over the land.

**7** He gathered many captives
    and ruled over Gazara and Beth-zur and the citadel;
    he removed its uncleannesses from it,
    and there was no one who resisted him.

**8** They tilled their land in peace,
    and the land gave its produce
    and the trees of the plain gave their fruit.

**9** Old men sat in the streets,
    all speaking together of good things;
    and the young men put on glorious and martial dress.

**10** He provided food for the cities
    and furnished them with means of defense,
    until his glorious name reached to the end of the earth.

**11** He brought peace to the land,
    and Israel rejoiced with great joy.

**12** Every man sat under his vine
    and under his fig tree,
    and there was no one to make them afraid.

**13** No enemy was left in the land to fight against them,
    and the kings were crushed in those days.

**14** He supported all the humble of his people;
    he sought out the law,
    and exterminated every lawless and wicked man.

**15** He made the sanctuary glorious
    and multiplied the sacred vessels.

---

**16** When news reached Rome and Sparta that Jonathan had died, they were deeply grieved.

**17** But when they heard that his brother Simon had become high priest in his place and was governing the country and its cities,

**18** they wrote to him on bronze tablets, to renew with him the friendship and alliance they had made with his brothers Judas and Jonathan.

**19** These were read before the assembly in Jerusalem.

**20** This is the copy of the letter that the Spartans sent: "The rulers and the city of the Spartans to Simon the great priest and to the elders and priests and the rest of the Jewish people, our brothers, greetings.

**21** The envoys sent to our people reported to us about your glory and honor, and we were glad at their coming.

**22** What they said we have recorded in the decrees of the people as follows: Numenius son of Antiochus and Antipater son of Jason, envoys of the Jews, came to us to renew our friendship.

**23** It was decided to receive these men with honor and to deposit a copy of their address in the public archives, so that the people of the Spartans might have a record of it. And a copy of this has been sent to Simon the great priest."

**24** After this Simon sent Numenius to Rome, bearing a large golden shield weighing a thousand minas, to confirm the alliance with the Romans.

**25** When the people heard these things, they said: "How shall we thank Simon and his sons?

**26** For he and his brothers and his father's house have stood firm and have repulsed Israel's enemies and secured their freedom." So they inscribed a record on bronze tablets and set them up on pillars on Mount Zion.

**27** This is a copy of the inscription: "On the eighteenth day of Elul, in the one hundred and seventy-second year — which is the third year of Simon the great high priest —

**28** in Asaramel, in a great assembly of priests and people and rulers of the nation and elders of the country, it was made known to us as follows:

**29** Since wars have often occurred in our land, Simon son of Mattathias, a priest of the house of Joarib, and his brothers exposed themselves to danger and resisted the enemies of their nation, so that their sanctuary and the law might be upheld; and they brought great glory to their nation.

**30** Jonathan rallied their nation and became their high priest, and was gathered to his people.

**31** Their enemies then sought to invade their country and stretch out their hands against their sanctuary.

**32** Then Simon rose up and fought for his nation and spent much of his own money; he armed the warriors of his nation and paid their wages.

**33** He fortified the cities of Judea, and Beth-zur on the border of Judea, where the arms of the enemy had been stored before, and he stationed a garrison of Jewish men there.

**34** He also fortified Joppa, which is by the sea, and Gazara on the borders of Azotus, where the enemy had previously been established, and he settled Jews there and equipped these cities with all that was needed for their restoration.

**35** The people took note of Simon's faithfulness and the glory he sought to bring to his nation, and made him their leader and high priest because of all this, and because of the righteousness and faithfulness he had maintained toward his nation, and because in every way he sought to exalt his people.

**36** In his time things prospered in his hands: the Gentiles were removed from their land, as were those in the city of David in Jerusalem who had built the citadel, from which they used to sally out and defile the precincts of the sanctuary, causing great harm to its purity.

**37** He settled Jews in it and strengthened it for the defense of the country and the city, and he raised the walls of Jerusalem higher.

**38** On account of this, King Demetrius confirmed him in the high priesthood,

**39** made him one of his friends, and honored him with great honor.

**40** For he had heard that the Romans had called the Jews friends and allies and brothers, and had received Simon's envoys with honor.

**41** The Jews and their priests resolved that Simon should be their leader and high priest in perpetuity, until a trustworthy prophet should arise,

**42** and that he should serve as their military commander and be responsible for the sanctuary and appoint officers over the public works and over the country and over the arms and the strongholds;

**43** and that he should take charge of the sanctuary; and that all public contracts in the country should be written in his name; and that he should be clothed in purple and wear a gold ornament.

**44** None of the people or the priests should be allowed to annul any of these decrees, contradict his orders, convene any assembly in the country without his permission, be dressed in purple, or wear a gold clasp.

**45** Whoever acted contrary to any of these provisions or contravened them should be liable to punishment.

**46** All the people approved the decree confirming Simon in these offices. Simon agreed and was pleased to serve as high priest and commander and ethnarch of the Jews and priests, and to be the protector of all.

**47** They gave orders that this inscription should be placed on bronze tablets and set up in the precinct of the sanctuary in a conspicuous place,

**48** and that copies should be deposited in the treasury, so that Simon and his sons might have them.
